title: Atomic batch record API
prompt: Build an in-memory HTTP record store. A record is {id,value,rev}: id is a string matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}, value a string of at most 200 characters, rev an integer that is 1 when the record is created and increases by 1 on every update. GET /records/:id returns the record or 404; GET /records returns 200 {items} ordered by id in code-unit order. POST /batch accepts exactly {operations}, an array of 1..50 operations, each one of {op:"create",id,value}, {op:"update",id,value,rev} or {op:"delete",id,rev}. First validate the whole batch shape: any malformed batch or operation returns 400 {error,index} (index of the first offending operation when applicable) and changes nothing. Then apply the operations in order against the current state, including effects of earlier operations in the same batch. An operation fails with 409 {error,index} when a created id already exists, when an updated or deleted id does not exist, or when rev differs from the current rev. If any operation fails the whole batch changes nothing; otherwise all changes are committed together and the response is 200 {results} with one entry per operation: {id,rev} for create and update and {id,rev:null} for delete. A record deleted and created again in a later operation or batch starts again at rev 1. No persistence or external services are needed.
